title: Why Web3 Payments Failed: Zero Gas Per Click via EIP-712 State Channels
caption:
Why did early Web3 crypto payments fail? 

Because nobody wants to wait 15 seconds for block confirmations or pay $0.20 in gas every time they read an article or query an API. 

Making 1 on-chain transaction per click was a fatal UX mistake.

Here is how A-Pay Protocol achieves ZERO gas per click with EIP-712 state channels. 🧵

The Architecture:
1. One-time Escrow Deposit: User or AI agent deposits $5.00 once into the Base Mainnet EscrowVault (0xd08c...ea16).
2. Off-Chain Micro-Tickets: Every subsequent click or API request signs an EIP-712 cryptographic promise in memory:
   • Gas cost: $0.00
   • Verification speed: 5 milliseconds
3. Batched L2 Settlement: The merchant server accumulates hundreds of signed tickets and settles them atomically in ONE single transaction on Base L2.

Result:
• 100x faster than credit cards
• $0.00 gas per click for users
• 0 chargeback fraud
• 100% non-custodial

The future of web micropayments isn't on-chain bloat. It's cryptographic state channels on Base L2. ⚡
